text:
ariel: Heads-up - we're seeing periodic TX drops on g8gn hosts in us-west-2 causing training pods to stall. Started ~02:30 UTC and has recurred every ~8-12 minutes. Any known driver/firmware gremlins?

sam: Which NIC/driver? any dmesg or ethtool output?

ariel: ENA driver on g8gn. Quick dmesg tail from one host:```
[1918765401.123456] ena 0000:00:03.0: Tx queue 2 timeout - resetting
[1918765401.123459] ena 0000:00:03.0: RX errors: 0, TX errors: 578
[1918765401.123462] nv_peer: pod eviction: network stalls
```

jess: ethtool -S shows TX queue descriptor stalls and skb retransmits:```
ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "tx_errors|tx_queue|tx_ring|tx_dropped"
tx_errors: 578
tx_dropped: 432
tx_queue_stall_count: 12
```

morgan: Firmware on affected nodes is ena-fw 2.8.3. We saw a similar pattern months ago with a different sku but that was fw 2.8.1. Could be regression.

ariel: Reproduced on fresh host after repro deploy, so not just a one-off. deploy-bot restarted the instance and it came back up but issue resumed after ~10m.

deploy-bot: automated-restart: instance i-g8gn-0a1 restarted at 1918765460 (canary).

sam: Can you capture a tcpdump during an occurrence? Also check MTU and offload settings (TSO/GSO/GRO). Those can hide retransmits on host side.

ariel: tcpdump shows bursts of retransmits and DUP ACKs during the drop window. MTU is 9000 across these clusters. Offloads are enabled by default. Snippet:```
15:02:10.123456 IP 10.0.8.12.54321 > 10.0.9.15.443: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12490, ack 98765, win 28960, length 145
15:02:10.124001 IP 10.0.8.12 > 10.0.9.15: ICMP 10.0.8.12 unreachable - frag needed and DF set
```

jess: ICMP frag-needed suggests MTU/DF mismatch when jumbo frames used. But the hosts are all set to 9000 and network path should support it. Could be firmware mishandling GSO segmentation.

morgan: Workaround idea: temporarily disable GSO/GRO on canary hosts and see if drops stop. Command: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off`

ariel: Applied to two canaries (g8gn-c1,c2). After disabling offloads, errors drop to near zero for ~30m. CPU went up a bit on rx-side but training pods are stable. This is promising.

sam: Good detective work. So likely driver/firmware interaction around GSO handling. File vendor ticket asap with: dmesg, ethtool -S, tcpdump, firmware version. Morgan can you open?

morgan: Opening AWS NIC support case. Attach logs and plan to roll firmware back to 2.8.1 on a small canary to compare. Case ref: AWS-2026-ENE-4589 (created).

ariel: For rollouts, propose: 3-host canary with offloads enabled -> monitor, then if fails, disable offloads cluster-wide as temporary mitigation. Also queue a fleet-wide firmware rollback if vendor confirms regression.

ops-oncall: FYI — scheduled maintenance window 23:00 UTC tonight for canary patching. I'll add a watch on the training clusters.

sam: Also add a Prom alert for sudden spike in tx_errors and tx_dropped per-host (threshold: >100 in 5m) and pod-network-latency >200ms. We didn't have a clear alert earlier.

ariel: Posted a short runbook in incidents: steps to collect logs and disable offloads. Putting it here:```
1) SSH to host
2) sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 50 > /tmp/dmesg.txt
3) sudo ethtool -S eth0 > /tmp/eth0-stats.txt
4) sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/capture.pcap
5) sudo ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off  # temporary mitigation
```

morgan: Vendor responded initial ack, asked for full pcap and list of impacted instance IDs. I've attached to the case.

ariel: TL;DR: g8gn + ena-fw 2.8.3 => TX coalescing/GSO bug causing ICMP frag-needed and retransmits with jumbo MTU. Workaround: disable host offloads until vendor patch or rollback. Rolling patch plan in place for tonight's canary.

sam: Thanks team. Keep updates here. If vendor provides firmware with fix, we'll coordinate Dedicated rollback and Private packaging.

ariel: Will update thread after canary completes (expected by 00:30 UTC). Thanks :thumbsup:
